# 0.0.0-dev.1: ???? (??-??-????)

## Breaking changes

- linkrot now requires Quarto 1.10 or later.

## Features

- `linkrot` identifies broken external links in Quarto documents during rendering.
- Configurable options include:
  - `fail-on-error`: Whether to fail the build on broken links.
  - `timeout`: Set the timeout duration for link checks.
  - `debug`: Enable detailed logging for troubleshooting.
  - `output-file`: Specify a file to write the link check report.
  - `skip-patterns`: Define patterns for links to skip during checks.
- Uses the `curl` command-line tool for robust link checking.
- Supports both HTTP and HTTPS links.
- `report-scope: project` collects the broken links of every page in a project
  in one `output-file` report, grouped by page. Re-rendering one page, for
  example in `quarto preview`, updates only that page's entry. The default,
  `report-scope: document`, writes a report for each document.
- linkrot names the page above its broken links, as in "Broken links in
  posts/news.qmd:", in the console and in `output-file`.

## Bug fixes

- `fail-on-error: true` now stops the render with exit status 1 when a link is
  broken, after the report is printed and written to `output-file`. Previously,
  Quarto logged the error but still wrote the output and exited 0, so CI
  builds passed.
- linkrot now passes each URL and the `user-agent` value to `curl` literally on
  macOS and Linux. Previously, a link containing `$(...)` or backticks ran that
  command while the document rendered.
- `timeout` now accepts fractional values such as `2.5`. Previously, they
  stopped the render with "number has no integer representation".
- linkrot now counts and lists each URL once, with its real status, even when
  it is linked several times. Previously, each repeat was added to the totals
  again and listed with the status "timeout/error".

## Documentation

- `skip-patterns` is now documented as a list of Lua patterns, not regular
  expressions, with examples that escape `.` and `-` with `%`. The earlier
  examples used a backslash, as in `example\\.com`, which is dropped when
  metadata is read as Markdown, so `.` matched any character.
- The README and FAQ now show "unavailable", the status linkrot reports when a
  link gives no response, instead of "timeout/error".
- The FAQ now explains that links are checked one at a time and once per output
  format, and that image sources and raw HTML links are not checked. Its GitHub
  Actions example now installs `coatless-quarto/linkrot`.
